title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We measure whether adding a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a generator–validator–repair, GVR, loop) around a single LLM (declared gpt-5-mini) increases the rate of correct, safely executable network configurations synthesized from natural-language intents versus plain LLM generation. In a fully preregistered paired design (cns-m2026-01) we processed 300 intents (600 episodes, shared-initial semantics). Baseline succeeded in 299/300 tasks (99.67%); guarded (validator ± one repair) succeeded in 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01]. The preregistered target (10 percentage-point absolute improvement) is not supported because the baseline generator was near ceiling. All model calls, provider traces, validator traces, per-episode scoring JSON, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 hashes (see Disclosure). We release full artifacts to enable reproducible follow-up on harder task distributions, multi-iteration repairs, or multi-model comparisons.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent-driven network automation (intent→configuration). Operational use requires that generated configurations satisfy the operator intent and do not introduce unintended reachability or safety changes. A common architectural pattern is a generate→validate→repair (GVR) loop that interposes a deterministic validator and a repair step around a generator. We designed a preregistered paired experiment to quantify the marginal benefit of a single-step deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair (cns-m2026-01). The study intentionally used shared-initial semantics so the same generator proposal is evaluated with and without the validator+repair stage; this isolates the gate's marginal effect on identical generator outputs. Our main confirmatory hypothesis (H1) asked whether the paired success rate (execution-validated correct configs) increases under the guarded pipeline. We archive all artifacts (model calls, provider traces, validator traces, per-episode scoring) and report exact counts and hashes.
sections.related_work: Prior work motivates verifier-assisted NetOps and intent→config evaluation (examples: NetConfEval and validation pipelines for network automation). Architectural proposals for proposer/verifier separation and closed-loop verification are widespread in recent LLM-agent literature (see cited_record_ids). Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered, paired measurement that quantifies the marginal effect of a single deterministic validator+one-repair gate on a controlled intent distribution and supplies full execution provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA-256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). Unit = intent (paired baseline vs guarded). N=300 intents deterministically selected (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). Inclusion/exclusion, contamination filters, and RNG seeds were preregistered and executed automatically; contamination-summary output is archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv; SHA-256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Model and calls: declared model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Shared-initial semantics: a single shared generator call produced the candidate used by both conditions; guarded then invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, if the validator rejected, at most one automated repair (preregistered repair budget). Validator and emulator artifacts: implementation pointers and the recorded transformation manifest (which lists the validator implementation and emulation images) are archived in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA-256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1); the execution manifest records full provider-call traces, response files, and scoring outputs (see execution manifest). Representative provider-call traces and prompt artifacts are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (examples: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json SHA-256 = cfd2d0956873ca732f5278c5d9bd64f0ffb008623d7fb52d2958c7769b69a791; execution/call_cache/017065ac823abfb3... SHA-256 = a632f9e9bbd3fff218e8cce95147832cbd707273573f31e1a21858cc42fbcff9). Emulation assumptions: the deterministic validator operationalizes safety as absence of unintended reachability changes in a closed-world emulator snapshot (validator traces archived per episode). Analysis plan: preregistered paired analysis (exact McNemar two-sided; bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All analyses run by the preregistered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts archived (analysis/*).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory results (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): complete_pair_count = 300. Baseline successes = 299/300 (99.6667%); guarded successes = 300/300 (100.0%). Contingency: n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Provider-call accounting (execution manifest) shows model_calls_used = 301, shared_initial_generation = 300, repair calls = 1; the single observed repair call is archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA-256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). Per-episode scoring JSON and validator traces (examples in execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/) document that the guarded pipeline corrected one validator-detected ordering omission (task-000117): baseline response and guarded repaired response files and their SHA-256 hashes are archived (execution/responses/task-000117-baseline.txt SHA-256 = 2422520c3cbfd26a45a7232100cdf5d4fb9ccc5e00c01f8ca4854499d13e7d70; execution/responses/task-000117-guarded.txt SHA-256 = 5f1dc27b7325694bfbd67caa42c06db285fdfc825d2a41d2039d9e28628b0e7d). Missingness: failed_episode_count = 0; no technical exclusions in primary analysis.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the GVR gate corrected one isolated generator mistake but produced only a +0.33 percentage-point aggregate change because the baseline generator was near ceiling on this deterministic task corpus. Operationally, this shows that a single-step validator+one-repair gate can fix individual errors (artifact-backed examples archived) but yields negligible measurable aggregate improvement when the generator already performs at near-perfect levels. Implications: measurable operational benefit of GVR loops requires either (a) lower baseline generator accuracy (e.g., human-authored or adversarial intents), (b) larger repair budgets (multi-iteration repair), or (c) substantially more challenging task distributions. H2 (that residual failures after GVR are primarily specification‑ambiguity) is untestable here because there were zero residual guarded failures; we therefore report H2 as preregistered but not assessable with the observed data. Threats to validity: internal—the shared-initial design isolates validator effect but does not evaluate alternative guarded-generation strategies; construct—the validator encodes closed-world reachability on the emulator (a pragmatic proxy for safety) and may not capture all field conditions; external—deterministic synthetic tasks limit generalization to noisy, human-authored production intents; conclusion validity—ceiling effect reduces the ability to detect large preregistered effect sizes. All scoring files, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis logs are archived and hashed to support independent inspection.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered paired study (N=300) the addition of a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair corrected one baseline error (299→300 successes). The preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) is not supported because the baseline generator already produced near-ceiling correct configurations on this task set. We publish complete artifacts (provider traces, responses, validator traces, scoring JSON, analysis artifacts) and hashes to enable reproducible follow-up work exploring harder distributions, multi-iteration repairs, or multi-model comparisons.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement — autonomous run provenance and artifacts

This paper reports an autonomous post-lock research run governed by Master Prompt v1 and the preregistration cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA-256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The exact initial master prompt immutable reference archived in the evidence bundle is provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Models and provider
- Declared LLM: gpt-5-mini. Configuration and parameters are archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider traces for shared-initial calls and repair calls are archived under execution/provider_calls/; representative shared-initial trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA-256 = cfd2d0956873ca732f5278c5d9bd64f0ffb008623d7fb52d2958c7769b69a791). Model-call cache examples are archived under execution/call_cache/ (example entry execution/call_cache/017065ac823abfb3...; SHA-256 = a632f9e9bbd3fff218e8cce95147832cbd707273573f31e1a21858cc42fbcff9).

Validator, emulator, and transformation manifest
- The deterministic validator and the emulation image(s)/Dockerfile(s) used during scoring are recorded in the transformation manifest execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA-256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1). That manifest enumerates the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation and the container images used for emulation; consumers of the artifact bundle can inspect execution/transformation_manifest.json to locate validator source and image paths and their recorded hashes. Per-episode validator-run traces and per-episode scoring outputs are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ (examples and SHA-256 values are cited in Results). The single automated repair observed in this run is archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA-256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba).

Preregistration and experiment control
- The preregistered design (cns-m2026-01) specified shared-initial semantics, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination checks, stopping rules, and the primary paired analysis (exact McNemar two‑sided plus bootstrap CI). The final task manifest executed is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). The contamination-summary output (analysis/contamination_summary.csv; SHA-256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222) records that the final set of 300 tasks passed the preregistered automated contamination filters.

Autonomy boundary and human role
- Human Research Director set the high-level topic family (Generative AI/LLMs for NetOps) and participated in pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsal only. After the autonomy lock, the system autonomously conducted literature review, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, artifact archiving, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revisions. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Technical restarts: the run completed with failed_episode_count = 0; retry policy (preregistered) allowed up to two automated retries for transient provider or container failures; all retries and provider-call events are logged under execution/execution_log.jsonl and the execution manifest.

Reproducibility pointers
- Principal artifacts (examples) and their SHA-256 hashes cited in the paper: execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e2...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (91564bb6...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (3421adb5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (55eacb88...), analysis/contamination_summary.csv (389227f0...), execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (4deb410d...), execution/responses/task-000117-baseline.txt (2422520c...), execution/responses/task-000117-guarded.txt (5f1dc27b...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (b6ba6a75...). The full execution/execution_manifest.json provides a complete hash manifest of all archived artifacts; the execution summary and reconciliations are authoritative and available in the artifact bundle.

Limitations of disclosure
- The transformation_manifest identifies the validator and emulator artifacts and their recorded hashes; consumers should consult that manifest to retrieve validator source and emulation image references. No external URLs are invented here; all referenced artifacts and SHA-256 values correspond to files archived in the supplied execution bundle.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline success = 299/300 limits detectable improvement; detecting the preregistered 10 percentage-point increase would have required substantially more discordant pairs.
Task scope: the task corpus was deterministically generated and emulator-based; external validity to noisy, human-authored, or adversarial real-world intent distributions is limited.
Model scope: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine-tuned variants.
Validator construct: safety was operationalized as "no unintended reachability changes" under the closed-world emulator; this is pragmatic but does not exhaust all operational risk modes.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt was allowed by the preregistration; multi-iteration repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
